subject: frostAxe
pitch:
Category: Fantasy weapon.
Subject: frost-forged battle axe.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
I'm reviewing the render for issues with the axe design—the haft looks too thin beneath the head, and the bronze root plate protrudes oddly on both faces, resembling a strange brown patch rather than blending into the blade.

thin at bottom but attaches fine, and the plinth-to-blade proportions check out okay. The blade itself feels flat and lacks the dramatic crescent shape of a true Freljord axe—I'm thinking the horns should sweep forward past the cutting edge instead of forming a plain D-shape, so I'll adjust the outline to make the crescent deeper and the horns more pronounced.

Looking at other soundness issues: the bronze root plate reads as oversized brown oval patches rather than a clean langet-style plate, though the root plate on the blade side and fluke plate on the haft side do overlap in a way that's visually plausible, just a bit too large.

Checking the back view, the emblem mirrors correctly with the blade on the left, and the snowflake texture plane faces the right direction. The loose accessories (frost motes, cord beads, rock clusters) seem fine, but the haft looks thin below the head, with a 0.03 radius blue section running down to the grip.

I want to thicken the haft slightly to 0.034, extend the grip wrap longer and lower, and add more decorative bands, plus reconsider whether the bottom needs a bronze ferrule where it disappears into the snow mound. The horn crystals near the top and bottom of the blade look appropriately placed, and from the side the blade reads as a thin edge-on column with a glowing inlay strip and rows of white studs down the center.

Looking at this again, the overall silhouette reads too much like a glowing sword rather than an axe — the blade feels flat and dark, and the haft is too top-heavy. I want to reshape the crescent with sharper, more extended horns and a bulging edge curve at the center, which means adjusting the edge rim curve, horn crystal placement, and stud rows to match the new outline.

Adjusting outline coordinates...

Still adjusting crystal positions...

I'll need exact search strings for the edits: updating the bladeOutline block and the edge rim catmull line, while also considering haft thickness, bronze socket, and fur collar details.

For the remaining edits, I'm locating the topEdge line, horn crystal coordinates, and the haft's grip rod dimensions — adjusting the grip radius from 0.037 to 0.04 and length to 0.78, then updating the band positions along the haft.

Now I'm working through the stud and rune strip placement so they don't overlap with the fur collar or socket — repositioning studs to two rows at y 0.43 and 0.62, and testing whether rune strips fit better around y 0.79 given the grip length and fur collar position around 0.85-0.88.

I'll apply radius 0.046 uniformly across those band positions, bump the studs from z 0.04 to 0.045, and then carefully write out the exact edits line by line.
